About Mercor

Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world application. We’re solving problems few companies have encountered, with the opportunity to influence what the world’s most advanced AI systems become capable of doing. We’re looking for people who bring different perspectives, take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and hold themselves to an exceptionally high standard. You’ll have the opportunity to do consequential work alongside talented colleagues who challenge one another, collaborate openly, and share a commitment to excellence.

Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.

About the Role

As a Data Science Intern at Mercor, you’ll join a fast-moving, metrics-driven engineering team whose work shapes decisions across the company. You’ll analyze data that directly affects ranking, hiring efficiency, candidate experience and revenue, work with production datasets from your first week, and ship insights that product and engineering act on.

You’ll start on the analyses and tooling your team has wanted but hasn’t had the hands for, and as needs come up you’ll take deep ownership of them, with a named mentor alongside you. You’ll move quickly while keeping a high bar for analytical rigor, clarity and statistical correctness.

Where You’ll Work

Interns start on a rolling basis, so summer, spring and fall terms all work. About three weeks before your start we’ll match you to one of two teams:

- Product Data Science. The data science function for the marketplace and talent platform: metrics for matching, ranking and hiring efficiency, event instrumentation and data integrity, experiments on the candidate and customer experience, and scoring models that change who gets surfaced for which role.

- Applied AI Data Science. The data science function inside the org that delivers human data and evaluations to frontier AI labs: operational analytics for live customer projects, automated quality control that gates what ships, and evaluation science that shows a lab where its model breaks and why.

What You’ll Work On

- Defining north-star metrics and feature-level KPIs for ranking, interview analytics and payouts

- Designing A/B tests and quasi-experiments and turning results into product decisions within days

- Building dashboards and lightweight data models so teams can self-serve insights

- Instrumenting events with engineers and improving data quality, observability and latency

- Prototyping models, from baselines to gradient boosting, to improve matching and scoring

- Evaluating LLM-powered systems through rubric design, human-in-the-loop experiments and guardrail testing

What We’re Looking For

- Pursuing a degree in a quantitative field, graduating 2027 (potentially 2028)

- Strong fundamentals in statistics, SQL and Python

- Experience with experiment design, causal reasoning and data analysis

- Clear communication with engineers, product managers and leadership

- Curiosity about LLM evaluation, retrieval, ranking or marketplace dynamics

- Excited to work in person in San Francisco

- Nice to have: dbt, dashboarding tools, recommendation or search metrics, LLM and agent evaluation

Why Mercor

- Impact: your work powers how frontier AI labs train and deploy their models

- Learning: early exposure to frontier AI research and engineering

- Growth: a high-velocity team where interns ship to production

Compensation and Benefits

- $10K housing bonus if you live within 0.5 miles of our office during your internship

- $1.5K monthly stipend for meals/rideshare

- Health, dental and vision insurance

- 401(k) eligibility

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

As a Deployment Strategist Intern, you'll work as part of a diverse, generative, and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most important problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into a cohesive understanding of what the problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be. The problems you'll solve will require a curious and analytical mindset, a sharp intuition for product, an ability to speak the language of data, and an understanding that humans should make decisions.

At its core, this role is about uncovering dots and—without knowing the shape they form—figuring out how to connect them. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Horizon3.ai is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find, fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers & operators, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

An Overview

We're looking for Research Interns to join Horizon3 AI Research and work on technical problems at the intersection of super intelligence, systems security, and agentic systems for security.

You'll work on a concrete research problem with researchers and engineers at Horizon3. Depending on the project, this may include AI agents for security, autonomous pentesting, attack-path reasoning, cyber deception, AI safety and security, security evaluation of AI systems, or new methods for reasoning over security data and environments.

This is a hands-on research internship. You will not only study a problem or read the relevant literature; you will also build, experiment, analyze results, and communicate what you learn. Projects may involve research prototypes, experimental infrastructure, AI models or agents, security test environments, attack graphs, system telemetry, or other technical artifacts.

We do not expect every intern to arrive with expertise in both AI and systems security. You should have strong computer science foundations, meaningful experience in at least one relevant technical area, and genuine interest in developing expertise across AI and security.

Interns will receive mentorship and technical guidance throughout the summer, but we also expect curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to investigate difficult technical questions independently.

What You’ll Do

- Work on a defined research project at the intersection of AI, cybersecurity, and computer systems.

- Understand the research problem, relevant technical background, and existing approaches.

- Read and critically evaluate academic papers and technical material related to the project.

- Develop and implement research ideas, algorithms, prototypes, or experimental systems.

- Design and run experiments to evaluate research hypotheses and technical approaches.

- Analyze experimental results carefully and identify limitations, failure modes, and unexpected behavior.

- Work with security data and environments that may include attack paths, graphs, telemetry, configurations, identities, networks, cloud systems, or security controls.

- Collaborate with Horizon3 researchers, security engineers, attack engineers, and other technical teams as appropriate for the project.

- Document methods, experiments, and findings clearly so that the work can be reproduced and continued after the internship.

- Present research progress during the internship and communicate final findings to the broader team.

- Contribute, when appropriate, to research outputs such as technical reports, prototypes, open-source artifacts, patent disclosures, or academic publications.

What You’ll Bring

- Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent technical experience.

- Strong computer science fundamentals and programming ability.

- Experience or demonstrated interest in systems security, super intelligence / machine learning, computer systems, or a closely related area.

- Ability to translate technical ideas into working implementations.

- Ability to read technical material and learn unfamiliar concepts independently.

- Curiosity about difficult technical problems and willingness to investigate why a system behaves the way it does.

NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

Job Description

The Advanced Computing Solutions Group in the Computational Science Center at the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) has an opening for a graduate student researcher in connected and automated vehicle communications modeling, with an emphasis on data analysis and machine learning.

Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication lets vehicles talk to each other and to roadside infrastructure, and it is the backbone of cooperative driving automation. Field-testing V2X at the scale needed to see its effect on traffic would take hundreds of roadside units and thousands of equipped vehicles, which is cost-prohibitive, so simulation is the practical path.

The intern will work with NLR colleagues to analyze field V2X data and develop new V2X models for simulation.

We are looking for a motivated researcher with strong data and programming skills and an interest in the mission of NLR. The successful candidate will collaborate with NLR researchers.

Responsibilities include:

- Clean, process, and analyze large-scale V2X field-test logs to characterize communication performance (e.g., packet delivery ratio, latency, and range) as a function of distance, device density, and environmental conditions.
- Help calibrate and validate microscopic LTE-V2X communication models against the field-test data.
- Develop and train machine-learning surrogate (approximate macroscopic) models of V2X behavior from large sets of simulation data, and evaluate their accuracy and computational efficiency.
- Write well-documented Python code and run workflows on NLR’s high-performance computing systems.
- Document results and contribute to technical reports, presentations, and publications.
